gaps.sentence: It's ___ eight o'clock news — hurry up!
gaps.explanation: 'The eight o'clock news' — a specific, known programme.

gaps.sentence: It was ___ best meal I've ever had.
He demands ___ answer before the end of the day.
She spent three weeks in ___ hospital after the accident.
gaps.explanation: British English: be in hospital (as a patient) takes no article; the building is the hospital.

gaps.sentence: She's studying history at ___ University of Vienna.
gaps.explanation: University names with of-phrases take the: the University of Vienna.
'The courage he showed' — the relative clause makes it definite.

gaps.sentence: My uncle is ___ university lecturer and a painter in his free time.
gaps.explanation: 'A university lecturer' (the u sounds like /juː/); the second gap is also 'an artist'.

gaps.sentence: It's ___ one-way street, so you can't turn left here.
gaps.explanation: 'One' starts with /w/, a consonant sound, so 'a one-way street'.
